# Anchor: schema_spec_format

> Description: Defines the canonical 2-section format for all Purlin specs: Rules and Proof.
>   The `sync_status` tool parses specs against this format and reports violations as warnings
>   or missing coverage.
> Scope: specs/**/*.md

## Rules

- RULE-1: Every spec MUST contain exactly two required sections: `## Rules`, `## Proof`
- RULE-2: Rules are numbered sequentially as `RULE-N` (RULE-1, RULE-2, ...). Unnumbered lines under `## Rules` trigger a sync_status WARNING
- RULE-3: Proofs are numbered as `PROOF-N (RULE-N)` — each proof references the rule it covers
- RULE-4: Every RULE must have at least one corresponding PROOF
- RULE-5: `> Requires:` metadata, when present, is a comma-separated list of anchor names whose rules also apply to this feature
- RULE-6: `> Scope:` metadata, when present, is a comma-separated list of source file paths the feature touches
- RULE-7: Feature specs use heading `# Feature: <name>`, anchor specs use `# Anchor: <name>`
- RULE-8: `> Description:` metadata, when present, is a plain-language summary of the spec; supports multi-line via `>` continuation lines that do not match a metadata field pattern (`> FieldName:`)
- RULE-9: A proof line may end in a tier tag `@<tier>` and a platform tag `@on(<platform-id>[, ...])`, in either order, at most one of each; a tag is recognised only when it does not follow a list connector (`,`, `and`, `or`), so prose that merely ends in an `@word` is not a tag. `@on` names the platforms the proof must be proved on; a proof without it is platform-agnostic. `@on` alone means tier `unit`; `@on` on a `@manual` proof is ignored with a warning; a bare `@windows` tier is read as `@unit @on(windows)` with a warning naming the rewrite. `scripts/mcp/purlin_server.py` and `scripts/audit/static_checks.py` each carry a character-identical `_TIER_TAG_BODY` pattern and `_split_proof_tags` helper, because the two modules are independent and a shared import would couple the CLI to the server
- RULE-10: A platform id matches `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*`, because it appears in a proof filename, a workflow name and an environment variable; an id containing a dot, an underscore or an upper-case letter is rejected with a warning and dropped from the proof's platforms rather than silently accepted
- RULE-11: `> Note:` metadata, when present, is free text addressed to whoever reads the spec (setup a checkout needs, why a `> Source:` points where it does). The parser ignores it: it is never folded into `> Description:` (it matches the `> FieldName:` pattern that ends a description continuation), never read as `> Source:`, `> Scope:` or any other field, and a spec may carry more than one

## Proof

- PROOF-1 (RULE-1): Parse `references/formats/spec_format.md`; find the `## Required Sections` area; verify both sections (`## Rules`, `## Proof`) appear within it
- PROOF-2 (RULE-2): Create a spec with an unnumbered line under `## Rules` (e.g., `- some constraint without RULE-N prefix`); run sync_status; verify it reports a WARNING about unnumbered rules
- PROOF-3 (RULE-3): Grep `specs/**/*.md` for lines under `## Proof`; verify every proof line matches the pattern `PROOF-\d+ \(RULE-\d+\)`
- PROOF-4 (RULE-4): Create a spec with RULE-1 but no PROOF referencing RULE-1; run sync_status; verify it reports the rule as uncovered @integration
- PROOF-5 (RULE-5): Create a spec with `> Requires: base_anchor`; run sync_status; verify the report includes `base_anchor/RULE-1` in the coverage output @integration
- PROOF-6 (RULE-6): Create a spec with `> Scope: scripts/mcp/purlin_server.py`; verify sync_status parses and displays the scope files @integration
- PROOF-7 (RULE-7): Grep `specs/**/*.md` for first-level headings; verify each starts with `# Feature:` or `# Anchor:`
- PROOF-8 (RULE-8): Create a spec with `> Description: First line\n>   second line\n> Scope: src/`; parse description; verify it equals "First line second line" (continuation joined, Scope not included)
- PROOF-9 (RULE-9): Call `_split_proof_tags` in both `purlin_server` and `static_checks` with `@unit @on(windows-2022)`, `@on(windows-2022, macos-14) @integration`, `@on(windows)` alone, `@manual @on(x)`, a bare `@windows`, and prose ending `, and @windows`; assert both modules return identical `(clean_desc, tier, platforms, warnings)` tuples, that the clean description carries no `@` tag, that `@on` alone yields tier `unit`, that `@manual @on(x)` yields platforms `[]` with one warning, that bare `@windows` yields tier `unit`, platforms `['windows']` and the warning `write @unit @on(windows)`, and that the prose case yields no tag and an untruncated description; fails when either module's `_TIER_TAG_BODY` differs from the other's
- PROOF-10 (RULE-10): Call `_split_proof_tags` in both modules with `@unit @on(Windows_2022)`, `@unit @on(ubuntu-24.04)` and `@unit @on(windows_2022)`; assert each returns platforms `[]` and exactly one warning naming the rejected id, while `@unit @on(ubuntu-24)` returns `['ubuntu-24']` with zero warnings; fails when the id pattern admits `_`, `.` or an upper-case letter
- PROOF-11 (RULE-11): Write an anchor spec carrying `> Description: Local policy`, then `> Note: run bash dev/setup-external-refs.sh before the first sync`, `> Source: ./dev/external-refs/policy.git` and `> Pinned: d1e2816`; call `_scan_specs`; verify the feature parses with `description` equal to `Local policy` and `source_url` equal to `./dev/external-refs/policy.git`, and that the string `setup-external-refs` appears in no parsed value of that feature; a parser that folded the Note into the description or the Source fails @integration
